tob-10228: Eighty-one short chapters make up the Tao Te Ching, the founding text of Taoism attributed to the sage Lao Tzu. Its verses praise the quiet power of water over stone, warn against ambition, and counsel rulers and commoners alike to follow the natural way. This is James Legge’s translation, among the first to bring the work to English readers. Its wisdom has guided China for millennia.
tob-10628: The blind Syrian poet Abu al-Ala al-Ma’arri was one of the boldest freethinkers of the medieval Islamic world. His poems mock superstition, pity the folly of rulers, and preach kindness to all living things — centuries before such ideas were fashionable. This Diwan gathers his verses in English, preserving the voice of a lonely genius.
tob-10828: The third volume of Blavatsky’s Secret Doctrine collects her writings on occultism and the esoteric side of religion — magic, symbolism, and the hidden history of spiritual traditions. Published after her death from her papers, it is less systematic than the first two volumes but rich in provocative ideas. It completes the most ambitious work of modern occultism.
tob-4028: Immanuel Kant’s Critique asks what the mind can and cannot grasp — and finds that we can know the world we meet, but never things as they are in themselves. This flip in outlook wedded science to morals and faith. Hard going but world-shaking, it is the key work of modern thought.
tob-9028: Saint Augustine’s City of God, penned after Rome’s sack in 410, stands up for the faith against pagans who blamed it for the empire’s fall. Through twenty-two books he sets the city of man against the city of God, braiding history, thought, and scripture. Marcus Dods’s rendering remains the go-to English version.
tob-4128: G. R. S. Mead’s 1896 Pistis Sophia first opened the great Gnostic gospel to English eyes. His learned foreword sets the risen Christ’s hidden teaching amid the lost Christianities. Scholars and seekers alike owe Mead a debt. The volume made him England’s trail-blazer in Gnosis-study.
tob-13328: Ralph Griffith’s Ramayana gives Valmiki’s great king-tale — Rama’s forest-faring, Sita’s stealing by Ravana, and the great war. His 1870 verse-Englishing bore India’s beloved tale to our readers. The epic’s high heart and ruth have stirred readers two thousand years.
cia-0000111428: Zaire: Is It Reformable? — a study estimated to date from May 1980 on Mobutu's corrupt, crumbling Congo. American aid propped up the dictator as a Cold War ally while his country rotted. The blunt title asks the question Washington kept dodging: could this regime ever be fixed, or was the money wasted?
cia-0000112828: A September 1945 summary of information on W. Schmalfuss — another piece of the scattered dossier on this suspect. Summaries like this one distilled everything known into a single reference. The entry shows the methodical side of counterintelligence: collect, summarize, file, repeat.
cia-0000119728: A September 1956 report of an imminent Soviet troop withdrawal from Hungary. The rumor of withdrawal — true, then reversed — was the revolution's emotional roller coaster. The document shows how desperately both Hungarians and Western observers clung to signs of Soviet retreat.
cia-0000124328: A June 1953 report on a prisoner-of-war camp at Tientsin, China. As the Korean armistice approached, every camp's roster mattered for the prisoner exchanges. The document is one facility in the vast exchange machinery — the paperwork of homecoming.
cia-0000126928: A June 1994 report on volcanic activity in the humanitarian relief zone of eastern Zaire. As Rwandan refugees flooded the region, a volcano added natural disaster to human catastrophe. The document layers crisis upon crisis — geology compounding genocide's aftermath.
cia-0000132228: Situation Report 545 on political and economic developments, with details on something the truncated title withholds. By the report's numbering, the war was deep into its decisive phase. The entry is the daily ledger: politics and economics, tallied while bombs fell.
cia-0000132428: A January 1960 report on Castro's chief economic planner outlining trade and investment plans — the truncated title suggests the scope. The revolution needed an economy to match its politics. The document is the blueprint: the planners, planning.
cia-0000132628: A June 1960 report with a vivid title: The Cuban Pot Boils Over. The metaphor said what analysis struggled to: the crisis was coming to a head. The document is the boiling point: the pot, overflowing.

cia-0000136028: The LINCOLN situation report for the week of March 15 to 22, 1954. Another week, another sitrep. The document is the watch: the week, covered.

cia-0000136228: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for CADICK/ONTRICH on operational readiness — but factors dictating delay, the archive's spelling says operatinal, the truncated title cuts off the rest. Ready, but waiting. The entry is the readiness: the force, prepared — the order, withheld.
cia-0000136328: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for ONTRICH recommending that Calligeris declare independence — the truncated title cuts off of what. The exile leader was urged to proclaim. The document is the recommendation: the declaration, urged.

cia-0000137328: The NSC briefing of March 10, 1960, with an attached document on a subject the truncated title withholds. The early-spring session. The document is the briefing: March's, recorded.

un-ga-res-a-69-28: General Assembly Resolution A/69/28, adopted in 2014. The twenty-eighth act. The designation and year align; the content awaits the reader.
un-sc-res-128: Security Council Resolution 128, adopted in 1958. The Council's business rolled on. The number and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.

un-sc-res-1028: Security Council Resolution 1028, adopted in 1995 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
cia-0000135628: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135628. The invasion year's documents. The document is the collection: the brigade, preserved.
cia-0000135728: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135728. The Bay of Pigs papers, another volume. The entry is the volume: the papers, bound by number.
cia-0000136728: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136728, the archive's date uncertain. The roughly dated set. The document is the roughness: the date, soft.
plos-pone-0000028: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper: perceptual learning of motion leads to faster flicker perception. Training your eyes on moving patterns makes you see flicker faster. The paper is the training: the perception, sharpened.
cia-0000139028: A 1946 CIA military information file on Russian activities, numbered 0000139028. The watching brief. The entry is the watch: the activities, noted.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d28: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, August 26, 1943 — Document 28. Late August, Washington to London. The message is the link: the allies, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d128: Minutes of the president's meeting with the Joint Chiefs of Staff, November — the truncated title cuts off the day — Document 128. The war's planners, minuted. The minutes are the planning: the chiefs, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d228: A memorandum by the United States Chiefs of Staff, November 18, 1943 — Document 228. Another planners' paper. The memo is the paper: the chiefs, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d328: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, November 26, 1943 — Document 328. The president wrote Moscow. The message is the letter: the president, to the marshal.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d428: The President to the ambassador in Turkey, Steinhardt, December 2 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 428. The White House answered. The message is the answer: the president, to Steinhardt.
arxiv-2605-08928: Generative models that must obey physical laws — soft constraints rather than hard rules — need mathematics that can handle both. Samer El Boustany, Samy Mekkaoui, Yadh Hafsi, and colleagues learn such dynamics through McKean-Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equations. The 2026 paper is stochastic analysis in service of physics-respecting generation.
arxiv-2605-09128: AI collectives need constitutions — rules for how agents decide together — and there are two ways to write them: deliberate design or evolved emergence. Hershraj Niranjani, Ujwal Kumar, and Phan Xuan Tan compare internal deliberation against external evolution for multi-agent constitutional design. The 2026 paper is political philosophy for robot societies.
arxiv-2605-09228: Helpful assistants do more than asked — they anticipate. Sepehr Harfi Ahmad Salimi, Dongming Shen, and Alex Smola introduce ProactBench, a benchmark for proactivity: going beyond what the user asked for. The 2026 paper measures whether AI assistants take useful initiative well.
arxiv-2605-09828: Middle convolution transforms differential equations and the structures around them; for Lie algebra representations it opens genuinely new territory. Kazuki Hiroe develops middle convolution in this algebraic setting. The 2026 paper is representation theory with a classical tool cleverly repurposed here.
arxiv-2605-10028: Turbulent flame combustion models in large-eddy simulation are expensive; hybrid in-situ machine learning accelerates them. S. Trevor Fush, Israel J. Bonilla, Michael B. Schroeder, and colleagues build Neural-ISAM for manifold-based combustion models. The 2026 paper is combustion modeling with neural speed.
plos-pone-0003428: Gut surgeons found a surprisingly fast self-repair in this 2008 medical paper. When blood flow to the human intestine is cut off and restored, a condition called ischemia-reperfusion, the damage looked severe at first. But the gut shed its injured lining cells within hours and recovered rapidly, a built-in healing response relevant to surgery and critical care.
plos-pone-0003528: Structural biologists solved two pieces of the cell's shipping dock in this 2008 paper. The signal recognition particle, or SRP, grabs newly made proteins destined for membranes, and the team determined the structures of SRP54 and SRP19, the proteins organizing its RNA core. The atomic pictures reveal how the universal protein-delivery machine is assembled.
plos-pone-0003628: Psychologists Dyck, Winbeck, and Leiberg tested whether digital faces fool human emotion readers in this 2008 study. Volunteers recognized emotions in natural versus computer-generated virtual faces, and the comparison measured how well avatars convey feelings. The results guide the use of virtual faces in psychology experiments and therapy.
plos-pone-0003728: In 2008, Molla-Herman, Boularan, and Ghossoub tracked a signal protein to the cell's antenna. Beta-arrestin2 was found at the centrosome and the primary cilium, the cell's sensory bristle, where it helps control cell division. The placement links a classic signaling player to the organelle that senses the cell's world.
plos-pone-0003828: In 2008, a team traced the weapon kits of a crop killer. Xanthomonas bacteria, which sicken over 390 plant species, were found to gain and evolve clusters of pathogenesis genes. The study maps how these gene clusters assemble, pointing to what makes each strain attack its chosen hosts.
plos-pone-0003928: In 2008, Field, Johnston, and Gati mapped a midbrain hub's wiring in monkeys. They zapped the superior colliculus with microstimulation while watching the whole brain with fMRI. The combined method traced the hub's connections without any chemical tracers. The connectivity map shows how this ancient structure talks to the modern brain.
plos-pone-0004028: In 2008, Chotpitayasunondh, Thisyakorn, and Pancharoen tested two bird-flu shot recipes. The trial compared safety and immune responses to two inactivated split-virion H5N1 formulations. Both antibody and T-cell responses were carefully measured in adult volunteers. The head-to-head data will inform future pandemic vaccine stockpiling plans.
plos-pone-0004128: In 2009, a team compared old gene tests by their pathways. Pathway signatures grouped similar gene-chip runs as close kin. The clever method tamed public data overload by matching pathway fingerprints. Shared marks revealed hidden kinship between far-flung lab studies fast.
plos-pone-0004228: In 2009, Bezuidenhout, Roberts, and Muller linked early HIV to hotter TB. Pleural tuberculosis in early HIV infection raised TNF-alpha expression sharply. The co-infected lung lining ran far hotter with inflammation. The finding explains faster TB damage in early HIV patients.
plos-pone-0004328: In 2009, a US team found stress retuning brain receivers. Stress and steroids shifted kainate receiver subunit mRNA in rat hippocampus. The glutamate receivers' blueprints changed fast. The finding links stress to synapse remodeling. The work maps stress onto memory wiring.
plos-pone-0358228: Students try AI learning apps — then many quietly quit. This paper moved beyond simple ‘responsiveness’ to model how product features, psychological needs, and enjoyment drive the intention to keep using AI learning tools. The differentiated results tell ed-tech designers what keeps learners coming back.
plos-pone-0358128: Tobacco mosaic virus RNA became an unlikely testbed for genetic signals. This paper detected bacterial gene expression elements on TMV RNA using cDNA analysis. The findings probe how gene-expression signals behave when placed on a viral RNA scaffold — basic science with synthetic-biology echoes.
plos-pone-0356528: Small poultry farms in developing countries lose birds to heat and disease they can’t see coming. This paper built an IoT system for automated early detection and real-time environmental monitoring for poultry farming. The cheap sensors give farmers an early warning before flocks sicken — and profits die with them.
plos-pone-0357828: Coastlines breathe carbon differently where two ecosystems meet and mingle. This paper showed cross-ecosystem subsidies drive CO2 flux rates in a coastal ecotone — the transition zone between habitats. The findings reveal how neighboring ecosystems feed each other’s carbon exchange, reshaping local climate math.
plos-pone-0355728: Coral restoration is only practical when local human pressure stays low — a sobering precondition. This paper showed that reef restoration efforts succeed meaningfully only where fishing, pollution, and coastal stress are already controlled. The finding redirects restoration money toward sites where it can actually work.
plos-pone-0356728: Awe — that vast, humbling emotion — proves surprisingly hard to induce reliably in the lab. This paper reports a series of replication attempts of experimental awe-induction effects. The replications test whether wonder itself can survive scientific scrutiny, with implications for the entire field.
plos-pone-0351328: Electronic health records tell a troubling story: progressive pulmonary fibrosis is undercoded, underrecognized, and undertreated with antifibrotic drugs. This EHR-based evidence exposes a threefold care gap — patients aren’t labeled, aren’t seen, and aren’t treated. The findings are a call to find these patients.
plos-pone-0352428: Breastmilk’s microbial ecology may influence whether infants develop iron deficiency anaemia. This Peruvian 16S rRNA metagenomic study linked breastmilk microbiota to infant anaemia in a mothers’ cohort. The findings suggest the milk’s microbes matter far beyond digestion.
plos-pone-0357028: Low vitamin D may literally make older adults fall. This cross-sectional study linked serum vitamin D levels to fall risk in adults using the Morse fall scale. The association strengthens the case for screening and supplementation as a fall-prevention strategy.
plos-pone-0355628: Blood sugar control and lung function decline together in type 2 diabetes — but how tightly? This systematic review and meta-analysis examined HbA1c’s relationship with pulmonary function. The pooled evidence reveals diabetes as a lung disease too — demanding that diabetologists mind their patients’ breathing.
plos-pone-0354028: Tropical slopes in Pagar Alam, Indonesia fail when rains come — but which slopes, and why? This paper studied rainfall-induced stability of unsaturated tropical slopes, testing slope gradient and soil layering effects. The findings guide landslide warnings for communities living beneath these hillsides.
plos-pone-0355828: Eurycoma longifolia — tongkat ali — does double duty against cellular decline. This paper showed it counters oxidative stress and unlocks autophagy to safeguard neurons and muscle cells. The dual mechanism lends scientific credibility to a traditional tonic — with implications for aging and neurodegeneration.
plos-pone-0342628: Liver cancer driven by metabolic risks — obesity, diabetes — is surging across East Asia. This paper quantified the disease burden and predictions across five countries from 1990 to 2023. The findings warn that metabolic liver cancer is becoming the region’s dominant oncologic threat.
plos-pone-0355228: Latinx caregivers living between two cultures — ‘viviendo entre dos culturas’ — need acculturation measured validly. This paper evaluated the psychometric properties of the Psychological Acculturation Scale among these caregivers. The validated scale honors the complexity of bicultural caregiving.
europmc-pmc2810828: When datasets have more measurements than samples, standard statistics break down. This 2010 paper presents sparse partial least squares regression, a method that shrinks dimensions and picks out the key variables at the same time. The authors show it handles wide data like gene expression cleanly. The technique became a staple for finding real signals in noisy, oversized datasets.
europmc-pmc2824828: In Parkinson's and related diseases, the cell's recycling system may fail at specific points. This 2010 paper finds selective changes in the autophagy pathway in patients with Lewy body disease and in models of alpha-synuclein buildup. The authors pinpoint which recycling steps go wrong. The specificity suggests targeted ways to restore the cleanup process.
europmc-pmc2871128: Muscles waste with age, and cell rust may drive it. This 2010 review links oxidative stress and molecular inflammation to sarcopenia, age-related muscle loss. The authors' overview connects chemistry to frailty. The review points to targets for keeping elders strong.
europmc-pmc2935128: Fish farming now feeds millions, and this 2010 paper surveys the surge. The authors review aquaculture's global status and trends across species and regions. Their stocktake reveals a booming industry with growing pains. The paper guides sustainable growth of the blue economy.
europmc-pmc2943128: Cell rust may sap male fertility. This 2010 review examines how oxidative stress and antioxidants affect semen function. The authors weigh the evidence for damage and defense. Their overview informs fertility care for couples. The findings shape advice on diet, smoking, and supplements.
europmc-pmc2978728: A pneumonia toxin trips the body's alarm bells. This 2010 paper shows pneumolysin sets off the NLRP3 inflammasome and drives fever signals without TLR4. The authors trace the trigger step by step. Their work explains pneumonia's immune storm. Blocking this path may calm severe cases.
europmc-pmc2990028: Global health training needs ethics rules. This 2010 paper sets ethics and best-practice rules for training stints in global health. The authors' rules protect host clinics and visiting trainees. Their work reshaped training programs. Voluntourism with scalpels drew the fire.
europmc-pmc3042628: Lupus needs mouse stand-ins, and this 2011 review surveys them. The authors cover the main mouse models of lupus. Their overview guides autoimmunity research. The work shaped drug testing. No single mouse mimics the human disease. The review matches models to research questions.
europmc-pmc3055228: Turmeric's compound may fight head and neck cancer. This 2011 review weighs curcumin's anti-tumor evidence in head and neck cancers. The authors sift lab and early human data. Their overview tempers hype with facts. Poor absorption remains the big hurdle.
europmc-pmc6515828: Salmonella sickens millions each year through contaminated food, yet different strains target different animals and people. This review dissects what makes the bacterium dangerous: the virulence factors that let it invade guts, dodge immunity, and survive in hosts from chickens to humans. Knowing these weapons helps design better vaccines, treatments, and food-safety measures.
europmc-pmc6523028: After the 2009 H1N1 pandemic, doctors noticed obese patients fared worse with flu - a pattern that had gone unrecognized. This review explains why: excess weight blunts immune responses to influenza A, worsens lung damage, and may even let the virus evolve faster. The findings matter for vaccination strategy and for protecting a growing share of the population each flu season.
europmc-pmc6661828: Plants under attack brew chemical weapons - secondary metabolites that deter pests and pathogens. This review explores how stress and defense signaling switches on their production. Understanding the triggers helps growers coax more protective chemistry from crops.
europmc-pmc6691128: The GAD-7 - seven quick questions about worry - is anxiety screening's workhorse. But does it really measure one thing? Testing its psychometric properties in a mixed psychiatric sample, researchers probed whether the scale holds together. The verdict strengthens trust in a tool clinicians use daily.
europmc-pmc6728328: Hydrogen peroxide is a green oxidant - if you can make it cleanly. This study steers oxygen reduction down the 2-electron path to H2O2 using single metal atoms on tailored supports, skipping the usual water endpoint. The selective electrochemistry could decentralize peroxide production.
europmc-pmc6736328: RNA sequencing reads the cell's active genes - but stitching the fragments into full transcripts is hard without a reference. rnaSPAdes assembles transcriptomes from scratch, purpose-built for RNA-Seq data. The tool helps researchers hear the full message in the chatter of short reads.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1128: GAO's 2007 report turns the audit lens on the China-watching commission — the small congressional shop tracking Beijing's rise. Its books, buys, and back-office habits needed tightening, GAO found. The report applies plain good-housekeeping rules to the very panel Congress built to keep an eye on America's top rival.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-528: Congress wrote cyber homework for the agencies — and GAO's 2007 report says several flunked it outright. The findings show departments stumbling over the law's data-defense chores, from patching to planning. The report's message is blunt: statutes do not secure servers; only people following them do.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-828: The Guard and Reserve were flying without a flight plan in 2007 — GAO's report says the Pentagon needed a real strategy and honest numbers for the citizen force. The findings demand transparency on the part-time troops. The report treats the reserve bargain as too big to run on autopilot.
openalex-w7207688228: Physical education in Brazilian public high schools faces a familiar problem: students who would rather sit out. This mixed-methods study asked students themselves what they think of PE class, then analyzed the answers to find what motivates or discourages them. The findings point to concrete ways teachers could make the subject more engaging. It treats student motivation as something to understand, not just complain about.
openalex-w7206201828: Medical school can feel sealed off from the community it serves, and university extension projects are meant to break that seal. This experience report argues that outreach work should start early in medical training, showing how it shapes students' education while bringing the university closer to society. Descriptive and first-hand, the article makes the case that community engagement is not an extra but part of becoming a doctor.
openalex-w7204933428: The pandemic pushed classrooms online overnight, and students have not logged off since. This scoping review surveys the literature from 2018 to 2025 on digital self-care in education: the teaching practices that help students use technology in balanced, healthy ways. The authors map what schools have tried and what the research supports. A timely overview for educators navigating the tension between screens as tools and screens as traps.
openalex-w7204269128: When disaster strikes with many victims, medics must sort the dying from the savable in seconds. This study looks at the START triage protocol in mass-casualty incidents: how it guides nurses and organizes the flow of care. The authors stress its role in chaos. A emergency-medicine study of order under the worst pressure.
openalex-w4416899828: Soil germs gave us most of our antibiotics, and they may hide more. This study used mass-spec scans to size up the untapped chemical promise of Actinomycetes. The team grew the case for hidden drug-making talent. A nature-drug study of microbes still keeping secrets.
pmc-13469728: In this 2026 lab study, researchers treated OVCAR-3 ovarian cancer cells with methotrexate and measured changes in Nrf2 and HO-1 proteins plus markers of programmed cell death. The results detail how the drug pushes cancer cells toward self-destruction at the molecular level. Work like this fills in the map of how chemotherapy actually kills tumors.
pmc-13467128: A 2026 critical review of methods for detecting hydrogen peroxide and superoxide in living mammals, covering the literature from 2015 to 2026. It looks hard at DCFH-DA — a widely used but flawed fluorescent dye — and evaluates better strategies. For cell biology, getting the measurement right matters because these molecules signal both health and disease.
pmc-13455628: In this 2026 medical imaging paper, scientists built a deep-learning system that reconstructs electroacoustic tomography images from a single view to monitor electroporation — the technique of opening cell pores with electric pulses, used in tumor treatment. Real-time imaging of the treated zone could make the procedure safer and more precise.
pmc-13451428: A 2026 expression of concern issued by a journal over a paper claiming MiR-124-3p protects against acute respiratory distress syndrome by targeting p65. Expressions of concern flag possible problems while an investigation runs, warning readers to treat the findings cautiously. This entry preserves the notice as published.
pmc-13438128: In this 2026 study, alcohol exposure disrupted the ghrelin system in lab experiments — impairing glucose sensing and boosting ghrelin secretion. Ghrelin is the hunger hormone, and the mechanistic work shows alcohol rewires appetite signaling at the cellular level. The findings connect drinking to metabolic disruption.
pmc-13433128: A 2026 veterinary oncology paper analyzing CpG, CHG, and CHH methylation — chemical marks on DNA — in the mitochondrial control region of dogs with malignant mammary tumors. Mitochondrial DNA regulation is an underexplored corner of cancer biology. The preliminary analysis opens a new line of inquiry in canine cancer.
pmc-13428728: A 2026 retrospective cohort study finding that high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions — precancerous cervical changes — often regress on their own in women aged 30 or younger. The natural history matters: overtreatment has real harms. The study supports watchful waiting for young patients.
pmc-13420328: This 2026 oncology paper used circulating tumor DNA to detect polyclonal KRAS resistance — multiple resistant clones at once — in lung cancer patients treated with adagrasib. Liquid biopsies that reveal the full resistance landscape let doctors adapt therapy. The study shows ctDNA catching what tissue biopsies miss.
pmc-13388028: This 2026 chemistry paper systematically studied how auxochromes — color-modifying chemical groups — affect fluorescence under varying temperature, pH, and viscosity, focusing on photo-induced electron transfer. Fluorescent probes are workhorses of biology, and the systematic data guide better probe design.
pmc-13360328: A 2026 systematic review and network meta-analysis comparing different forms of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia in adolescents. Teen sleep problems are widespread and CBT-I is first-line, but which format works best was unclear. The network analysis ranks the options.
pmc-13343728: In this 2026 Whitehall II study, metabolic syndrome predicted bidirectional transitions between frailty states — people moved toward and away from frailty depending on metabolic health. Frailty isn't a one-way street. The bidirectional analysis reframes aging as modifiable.
pmc-13329128: A 2026 cross-sectional study finding that an accelerometer-equipped running watch validly estimates peak vertical ground reaction force and cumulative weighted damage. Consumer wearables are entering biomechanics research. The validation supports their use in injury studies.
pmc-13439928: A 2026 correction notice for a paper titled "A bittersweet symphony: genetic insights into cider apple fruit quality." Corrections formally amend the published record. This entry preserves the correction as the journal issued it.
pmc-13525728: A 2026 real-world study of a topical Salvia fruticosa (Greek sage) leaf extract rich in carnosic acid and carnosol for facial seborrheic dermatitis, from mild to very severe. The plant extract's efficacy and safety were tested in practice. The natural product showed promise.
pmc-13448428: This 2026 conference abstract (CLTR-08) described treatment strategies for metastatic breast cancer patients with leptomeningeal disease in a prospective observational registry. The registry captured real-world care. The abstract summarizes the strategies.
pmc-13486628: This 2026 neurology paper refined electrophysiological criteria in CIDP and multifocal motor neuropathy — toward a unified definition of motor conduction block and proximal temporal dispersion. The diagnostic criteria were harmonized. The refinement aids diagnosis.
pmc-13431028: This 2026 orthopedic paper defined minimal clinically important difference, patient acceptable symptom state, and maximal outcome improvement values for a shoulder outcome measure (the title is truncated). The meaningful thresholds were established. The definitions aid interpretation.
pmc-13416228: In this 2026 study, chitosan supplementation and lifestyle changes affected health and gut microbiota in Icelandic females with obesity. The fiber intervention was tested. The effects are the finding.
pmc-13358428: This 2026 perspective paper addressed trauma and violence informed research and evaluation for mental health nursing. The trauma lens was applied. The perspective guides practice.
pmc-13369628: This 2026 correction notice amended a paper on toxic effects of copper and zinc oxide nanoparticles on brain antioxidant defenses in male Swiss albino mice. Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13441228: In this 2026 case report, a rapidly progressive painless acute aortic dissection was described. The silent dissection's speed was the danger. The case warns clinicians.
pmc-13569528: A 2026 comparative clinical evaluation of endothelin receptor antagonists in pulmonary arterial hypertension using a multi-criteria decision analysis framework (the title is truncated). The PAH drugs were systematically compared. The evaluation guides formulary choice.
pmc-13434928: In this 2026 23-year prospective cohort study, periodontitis was linked to all-cause mortality in 60- and 66-year-old individuals. The gum disease's death toll was quantified. The link demands dental attention.
pmc-13465128: This 2026 paper showed Caragana korshinskii tannin attenuated LPS-induced sheep rumen epithelial injury via TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling. The shrub's tannin protected the rumen. The attenuating is the mechanism.
pmc-13463928: A 2026 thoracic oncology paper: machine learning-driven radiomics for an early-stage predictive model of nodal upstaging. The AI predicted the lymph node surprise. The model is the surgical planning tool.
pmc-13424028: A 2026 paper on developmental dynamics of the ovine lung in health and cystic fibrosis at single-cell resolution. The sheep lung's development was mapped. The dynamics serve CF research.
pmc-13592928: A 2026 paper measuring perceived goal-concordant care among patients with advanced liver diseases and their caregivers. The care's alignment with goals was quantified. The measuring is the quality metric.
arxiv-2606-16028: In machine learning, one model often learns a shared representation used for many tasks. This paper studies, from an information-theory angle, how much shared representations help when the tasks are forced to stay "orthogonal" — not overlapping. The authors quantify the benefit mathematically, targeting theorists of representation learning.
arxiv-2606-16228: GRS 1915+105 is a star-hole — a small black hole — that blasts twin jets. Sky-watchers caught those jets aimed in odd, shifting ways, not the locked beams once hoped. This paper logs the find and weighs what could rock a hole's jets. For high-fire sky pros.
arxiv-2606-16828: CRIM is a natural game played on integer partitions — ways of splitting whole numbers into sums. This paper defines the game and analyzes it: who wins, and how. It is a combinatorial game theory paper for mathematicians who like their games rigorous.
